pages.text: A horizontal hall that turns $(l)Steam$() into FE, in $(l)three sizes$(). Steam piped into its ports spins up a big rotor; the rotor drives the generator. The scene shows the Small turbine.
$(li)The $(l)front and back$() are full squares; in between only the $(l)outer ring$() is shell, and the inside must be $(l)empty$(): that is where the rotor spins.

$(li)Use $(item)Turbine Casing$()s for the shell and put the $(item)Steam Turbine Controller$() $(l)in the middle of the front$(), facing out. The hall runs straight back from it.$(br)$(li)Swap any shell blocks for $(item)Turbine Port$()s: steam goes in, FE comes out. One port for a steam pipe and one for an $(l:cables/energy_conduit)Energy$(/l)

$(li)$(l:cables/energy_conduit)Conduit$(/l) is enough; the controller itself also gives power to cables touching it. Medium and Large turbines make more than a basic conduit carries: use $(l)Advanced$() conduits (16,000 FE/t) at a Medium one's ports and $(l)Elite$() ones (128,000 FE/t) at a Large one's. A Large one also takes more steam

$(li)than a basic $(l:cables/gas_pipe)Gas Pipe$(/l) carries (1,000 mB/t): use an $(l)Advanced$() one.$(br)Complete, the blocks disappear into one faceted $(l)enamel and mint octagonal hull$(): the controller becomes a panel on the front, every port a glowing hatch, and at the back you can see the $(l)rotor$(). A $(l:basics/multiblock_projector)Multiblock Projector$(/l) shows the layout of

any size in the world. Right-click the controller while it is unfinished and bigger drones fly out, each projecting a group of the blocks still to place; an amber X marks a block in the way. They start from the size you have built the most of (the Small one if none); each further click shows the next size, and after the Large

The rotor does not start at full speed: it $(l)spins up$() as long as there is steam, faster for small turbines than for big ones (5, 7 or 10 seconds by size), and $(l)spins down$() the same way when the steam runs out. The faster it turns, the more steam it uses and the more FE it makes. The rotor also stops when the
pages.title: Spinning up

pages.text: energy has nowhere to go, so no steam is wasted.$(br2)The GUI shows the steam tank (32,000 mB), the output, the rotor speed and the stored energy; hover the readout for the size's ratings. Right- click any block of the formed hall to open it.

A reactor makes 1 mB of steam for each unit of heat: a Medium tower with 4 rods at 300%, cooled with Coolant, makes 600 mB/t, just what a Medium turbine uses. If the turbines cannot keep up, the reactor's steam tank fills up and its core overheats.
